We intend to expand our SHOP segment through acquisitions of stabilized and lease-up communities, ground-up development through joint ventures, and strategic partnerships with high-quality operators in target markets.
We intend to utilize the cash flows and management fees from these JVs to support our seniors housing growth strategy.
We believe this demographic shift will support sustained demand for IL, AL, MC, and active adult communities of the type in which we invest.
Sustained home values and transaction activity in our target markets, particularly the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, can support affordability and move-in velocity at our communities.
We believe this shift in patient preference from inpatient to outpatient facilities will benefit our tenants as most of our properties consist of outpatient facilities.
We believe the trend towards physician group consolidation will serve to strengthen the credit quality of our tenants if our tenants merge or are consolidated with larger health systems.

Tariffs on imported building materials, appliances, and equipment have contributed to cost inflation for capital expenditure and renovation projects at seniors housing communities and may increase our development costs.

We expect SHOP to become a more significant component of our results as our communities continue to stabilize and increase occupancy and as we execute on our seniors housing acquisition and development strategy.

We expect to satisfy our short and long-term liquidity needs through various internal and external sources, including cash flow from operations, debt financing, sales of additional equity securities, the issuance of OP Units in connection with acquisitions of additional properties, select additional property dispositions and recapitalization transactions.
We have no other off-balance sheet arrangements that we expect would materially affect our liquidity and capital resources.
